extracted.intended_audience: general readers of 19th-century exploration travelogues; naturalists and maritime explorers
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive travelogue of a boat expedition exploring Australian rivers (Flinders, Albert) combining geographic measurements, natural history observations, encounters with Indigenous people, and reflective prose. The text records daily progress, navigational data, fauna/flora notes, and cultural remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise geographic and navigational record
rubrics_metrics.description: Record latitudes, bearings, distances, depths, widths, tidal behaviour, and other navigational details (e.g., "latitude 17 degrees 51 minutes South", depths in fathoms, widths in yards/metres, tides rise four feet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exact measurements and observations of tides, currents, bearings and distances so readers and future navigators can locate and evaluate discoveries; note changes (e.g., banks, shoals, submerged trees) and any impediments to progress. Examples from text: listing latitude, fathoms, widths, bearings, and noting tidal influence and ebb/flood rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid landscape and sensory description
rubrics_metrics.description: Use rich sensory imagery and simile/metaphor to evoke settings (moonlight, silvery stream, mangrove thickets, plains dotted with gumtrees, 'like another Narcissus').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance precise data with evocative prose to communicate atmosphere—describe light, sound (plash of oars, screeching vampires), color, and motion to immerse readers. Employ concrete images and occasional literary comparisons as in the passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural history documentation (flora and fauna)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record observed species with descriptive details and, where known, scientific names or provisional identifications (e.g., Hydromys chrysogaster; Eulabeornis castaneoventris), noting appearance, behaviour, abundance, and uses (food, sport).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide size, coloration, behaviors, eggs where relevant, habitats, and any specimen-collecting notes. Note local names and comparisons to known species; mention the utility of species (victualling) and hunting outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed account of expedition logistics and incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Document boat types, crew actions, provisioning, accidents, progress impediments (groundings, sunken trees), daily routine, and decisions (waiting for daylight, moving on with the gig).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include timings (night/day), temperature records, crew activities (cooking, watch), and problem responses (landing to inspect damage, selecting parties for land excursions) so expedition readers understand operational realities and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording encounters with Indigenous people and customs
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sightings and interactions with natives, their rites (e.g., burial tree containing a corpse, rite of circumcision), domestic activities (digging for warran), and responses to the explorers (watchfulness, fires to lure away).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what was observed with detail and restraint, note evidence rather than speculation, respect sacred places (avoid disturbing graves), and include ethnographic comparisons or references when appropriate. Also record actions taken (leaving presents, not disturbing the party).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrations, plates, and footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment text with sketches/plates and footnotes for views and explanatory material (numerous 'See the view annexed' and footnotes in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference attached views/sketches to clarify landscape or objects described; use footnotes to provide comparative or ancillary information (e.g., relating burial customs to other regions or sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and comparative reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine on-site observations with broader scientific or historical speculation (e.g., inferring former water-communications, comparing burial customs with Scythians, consulting Sir W. Hooker's soil judgement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualise local findings within wider natural-history, geological, or anthropological frameworks; when conjecturing, state degree of certainty and, where possible, cite other authorities or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming and documenting discoveries with justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign names to newly encountered geographic features and provide reasons/etymology (e.g., naming 'The Flinders' after a predecessor, 'The Albert' for royal loyalty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record naming decisions and any associated ceremonies or sentiments to establish provenance of names and connect discoveries to patrons, predecessors, or notable persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative pacing that alternates exploration, rest, and reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the narrative to alternate between active exploration (night/day travel, attempts to force openings), restful interludes (meals, fires, sleep), and reflective passages on scenery or feeling (pleasure at novel country, disappointment at being blocked).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these shifts to convey the emotional arc of exploration—hope, disappointment, exhilaration—and to give readers both action and contemplative context. Include chronological markers (dates, 'August 2') to track progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodical surveying technique and decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the process of choosing which branch to ascend, testing for fresh water (tasting), using leads, inspecting banks and islands, and deciding when to disembark for land exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the reasoning behind choices explicit (volume of water, direction, likelihood of leading inland), and report the methods used to test hypotheses (tasting water, sounding depths) so others can evaluate or replicate the survey approach.
